pages.text: $(thing)Fishing$() is a way of hunting the fish that swim around in rivers, lakes, and oceans. Fishing rods must be baited and cast. Fish attempt to eat the bait, and sometimes succeed. Reeling in a fish takes work, and becomes easier with higher level hooks.
First, you have to forge a fishing hook in an $(l:craftsmanship/anvils)Anvil$().

pages.title: Fishing Rod
pages.text: The fishing rod is crafted with a fishing hook.

Fishing rods are not useful without bait. $(t:#tfc:small_fishing_bait)$(6)Bait$() can be added to rods in a crafting table. To catch normal fish, you need $(thing)Seeds$() or $(thing)Shellfish$(). To catch $(t:#tfc:large_fishing_bait)$(6)larger fish$(), such as $(thing)Dolphins$() and $(thing)Orcas$(), you need $(item)cod$(), $(item)salmon$(), $(item)tropical fish$(), or $(item)bluegills$().

To release the bobber, $(item)$(k:key.use)$(). Wait for a fish to spot the hook and bite it. Then $(item)$(k:key.use)$() to pull it in. As you do that, the meter on your hotbar will fill up. Pull too quickly, and the fish will get away with the bait. Each time you fish, the fish has a chance of eating the bait. To catch the fish, pull it up on land and kill it with a tool or catch it with a $(l:agriculture/fishing#fishing_net)Fishing Net$(). You can hold the fishing rod in your offhand to make this easier.
The fishing bar replaces the experience bar when active.

pages.title: Fishing Nets
pages.text: Tired of hunting down fish with spears? Or losing a floppy catch while fishing? Craft a $(thing)Fishing Net$() to scoop up your dinner.$(br)To use a fishing net; $(item)$(k:key.use)$() on a fish entity to capture the fish into your inventory. Different tier fishing nets all act the same, but have different durability.
